## Roadmap / durable knowledge

- [ ] `ROADMAP.md` updated if status, evidence, sequencing, compatibility, or decisions changed
- [ ] Durable findings/experiments updated where applicable
- [ ] No secrets, proprietary artifacts, private user data, or huge captures were committed

### Process contract

- [ ] The PR has one primary bounded outcome.
- [ ] Claims match validation actually performed.
- [ ] New evidence that invalidated the plan is reflected in roadmap/docs rather than hidden by the implementation.
- [ ] Structured roadmap IDs/dependencies remain valid and acyclic when this PR changes roadmap sequencing.
- [ ] Evidence-producing CI/path filters cover the material producer/parser/schema/manifest/config dependencies that can change the validated result.

### Reverse-engineering evidence

- [ ] Established findings name evidence class and target/environment provenance.
- [ ] Validation or corroboration is independent of the derived mapping/model being validated, or is explicitly labeled internal consistency only.
- [ ] Serialized RE artifacts carry schema/input/producer provenance sufficient to reject stale or incompatible evidence.
- [ ] Ambiguous matches or correlations remain explicit; no arbitrary tie-break is promoted to identity.
- [ ] ABI/calling-convention claims used for argument interpretation or hook design are supported by observed target behavior where practical.
- [ ] Runtime experiments use a semantic success/failure oracle and explicit bounded termination contract rather than accepting generic activity as proof of the intended behavior.
- [ ] Harness/control capability evidence is not presented as target-specific runtime evidence.
- [ ] Negative results that prevent repeated dead ends are durable.
- [ ] Runtime behavior is not claimed from static or synthetic evidence alone.

### Blind-research provenance

- [ ] The active blind-research gate/boundary is defined by durable project-local policy or roadmap state rather than invented in this PR.
- [ ] Target-specific findings disclose provenance as `clean`, `contaminated`, or `external-assisted` (or the project's explicit equivalent) separately from evidence class.
- [ ] Accidental target-specific disclosure is recorded and potentially influenced conclusions remain contaminated even after independent correctness corroboration.
- [ ] Any pre-unlock external rescue links a prior durable blocker/negative result and a bounded maintainer unlock; dependent findings remain external-assisted.
- [ ] Post-blind external comparison preserves the independent result and reports agreements/disagreements separately rather than rewriting the blind record.
- [ ] Unsupported repository history or operator-provided target-specific recovered artifacts were not used as an undeclared shortcut.

### Proprietary target experiment safety

- [ ] Operator-supplied target/fixture inputs are identity-verified and left immutable; writable execution uses an isolated copy/overlay where needed.
- [ ] The detached machine-readable run record has an explicit supported schema/version and captures target/fixture, scenario/config, harness/tool, material environment, termination, semantic oracle, and artifact provenance without embedding proprietary payloads.
- [ ] Artifacts/logs are bounded and sanitize private paths, credentials, user identifiers, and unrelated host data.
- [ ] Ambiguous target or fixture selection fails closed rather than choosing a candidate silently.

### Binary compatibility and rollback

- [ ] Supported binaries/versions are identified precisely.
- [ ] Expected bytes/signatures/invariants are verified before patching.
- [ ] Unsupported or ambiguous targets fail closed.
- [ ] Install/remove/rollback behavior is documented and tested where applicable.

### Ascendancy validation and blind-RE disclosure

- [ ] For target-specific work while M1 is active, the PR states `clean`, `contaminated`, or `external-assisted`; any rescue links both the prior blocker/negative result and the dated bounded roadmap unlock.
- [ ] Documentation links/checks relevant to the change were run.
- [ ] Focused unit/fixture tests were run where applicable.
- [ ] Intended-architecture build was run where applicable.
- [ ] Pattern/patch validation tests were run where applicable.
- [ ] Install/remove/rollback behavior was tested where applicable.
- [ ] Target-machine validation is explicitly `performed`, `still required`, or `not applicable`; performed validation names the exact target SHA-256 and scenario.
